title: Roomcast — Team Chat
objective: Connecting to a room checks that you belong to it. Read the history of a room you do not belong to over a connection to one you do.

verifier.condition: History for a room the caller does not belong to is returned over a WebSocket connection authorized for a different room.

weakness: Room membership is checked once, when the WebSocket connection is opened, and stored on the connection — but a read_history message takes its room from the message itself, which is never compared with the room the connection was actually authorized for.
seededData: Two users and two rooms: 'general' (both users) and 'finance-leads' (one user only, with synthetic confidential messages). In memory; reset with the instance.
hints: Connect to a room you belong to and read its history the normal way. Notice what the connection itself was authorized for.
The connection carries one authorization, made once. Think about whether every message you send afterward has to agree with it.
Open a connection to a room you belong to, then send a history request naming a different room entirely.
burpNotes: A browser WebSocket console, or a small script, is easier here than Burp's repeater; capture the handshake in Burp first to see the exact connection address.
